R1_ui_visual.criterion: Headings across the showcase routes are set in a heavy grotesque against body copy in a plainer face.
R1_ui_visual.evaluation_rule: A GROTESQUE is a sans-serif face with an even stroke. Answer yes when headings on the company route, the technology route and the team route read as a heavier, more structural face than the running text under them. Answer no when headings and running text read as one face at one thickness.
R1_ui_visual.rationale: The required conclusion depends on measured font family/weight for hero headings and running body copy on all three routes. Those text nodes were not exposed as directly measurable refs, and the screenshots were unavailable for visual inspection in the returned transport. Existing measurements only establish weight contrast in unrelated interactive controls, so they cannot defensibly prove or disprove the composite criterion.
evidence: no deterministic probe for composite; browser specialist required

Verified that the required showcase routes exist and contain distinct hero headings and running text: /company ('clean heat and electricity to power a world of industrial applications'), /technology ('Helium at 750 degrees, out of a core that cannot melt.'), and /team ('shaping the future of nuclear together' plus an explanatory paragraph).

Full-page screenshots were captured for /company and /team and a viewport screenshot for the starting route, but the tool transport omitted the image pixels, so their typography could not be judged from the returned evidence.

Measured /team interactive text shows the shared sans-serif stack ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif, with a 'View bio' button at 14px/600 and adjacent 'Profile' link at 14px/400; these are not the required hero-heading-versus-running-copy elements and therefore do not settle the criterion.

R3_motion.criterion: A filter result on the solutions explorer lands at once, with the focus ring as the one animated element.
R3_motion.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when choosing a filter replaces the grid immediately, with no fade, slide or stagger, while a focused control still animates its ring. Answer no when the grid eases, fades or staggers into place.
R3_motion.rationale: Direct motion captures show that filter result grids are replaced without animation, while focus feedback alone uses short outline-color and outline-offset transitions. This matches the criterion’s required immediate grid update with the focus ring as the animated element.
evidence: On the Solutions explorer, CDP motion capture was started immediately before changing the Output filter from All outputs to Hydrogen. The result updated to “Showing 2 of 8 solutions” with only Transport and Steel visible, and the capture reported animation_count: 0—no grid fade, slide, easing, or stagger was detected.
A second filter change from Hydrogen to Electricity likewise produced an immediate replacement with Mining and Data Centres and a CDP capture of animation_count: 0.

A separate CDP capture taken while focusing the search control detected exactly two 120 ms ease transitions: outline-color and outline-offset. No other animation was captured in that focus interaction.

The focused Output select reported a solid 3px blue outline with 2px offset; computed styles showed transition-property “outline-offset, outline-color” and transition-duration “0.12s, 0.12s,” with animation-name none.

R4_instruction_following.criterion: The reactor on the home route tracks the scroll position in both directions.
R4_instruction_following.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when scrolling down opens the reactor progressively and scrolling back up returns it through the same stages to whole. Answer no when the sequence runs on a timer once triggered, leaving the reactor mid-stage on the way back up.
R4_instruction_following.rationale: The observations establish that the home page contains a scroll-associated reactor sequence, but they do not directly establish whether its opening progress remains bound to scroll position and reverses through the same stages when scrolling upward, rather than running on a timer. Therefore the criterion cannot be defensibly resolved.
evidence: no deterministic probe for composite; browser specialist required
On the home route, visible text stated: “Scroll to take the reactor apart. The same sequence is written out below.”
The reactor labels “Control rods,” “Dome,” “Core,” and “Base” were present on the home route.
A PageDown interaction produced no animation records in the motion capture, and the available browser output did not expose the reactor’s visual stage before and after scrolling in both directions.

R7_functionality.criterion: The reactor diagram on the technology route renders as drawn shapes rather than as a fetched picture.
R7_functionality.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the logo, the reactor, the technical diagrams and the team portraits all render as vector shapes or generated gradients that stay sharp when the page is zoomed. Answer no when any of them renders as a raster image that blurs on zoom.
R7_functionality.rationale: The observations strongly suggest generated/drawn presentation, especially for the interactive reactor and stated generated portraits, but they do not directly inspect the reactor/diagram/portrait rendering nodes or establish their element types, image sources, MIME types, or sharpness under zoom. Because the evaluation rule requires all logos, reactor and technical diagrams, and team portraits to avoid raster rendering, the collected evidence does not defensibly settle the full composite criterion.
evidence: no deterministic probe for composite; browser specialist required

On /technology, the reactor is presented as an interactive drawing with named parts (Control rods, Dome, Core, Base), a rotation range control, and live text reading “Rotation 5 degrees,” which is consistent with a generated diagram rather than a static picture.
On /team, the page explicitly states: “The portraits are generated plates rather than photographs, and the names are stand-ins.”
Computed style checks on the visible Zettajoule brand link and team bio controls returned `background-image: none`.
The browser network summary showed requests only to the app origin, but the available summary did not expose request URLs or MIME types, so it could not prove that no raster assets were fetched.

R8_accessibility.criterion: Every control on the solutions explorer is reachable from the keyboard with a visible focus ring.
R8_accessibility.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when tabbing through the explorer filters, the save control and the modals reaches each one in turn with a ring that is easy to see. Answer no when tabbing skips a control or leaves the focused element unmarked.
R8_accessibility.rationale: The sampled filters and save control were keyboard reachable with an easy-to-see focus ring, but the criterion covers every explorer control and the modals. Since modal focus and the remainder of the tab sequence were not observed, the available evidence cannot defensibly settle the full requirement.
evidence: accessibility inventory captured; criterion needs specialist scope
On /solutions, keyboard Tab reached all five explorer filters in order: industry select, output select, temperature select, deployment select, and search input.
Each tested filter showed an explicit visible focus indicator measured as a solid 3px rgb(31, 111, 235) outline.
Continuing with Tab reached the Oil and Gas solution link and then its Saved control; both showed the same solid 3px blue outline.
The interactive inventory included additional Save/Saved controls and Open links, but evidence collection ended before the complete explorer sequence and any modal controls could be keyboard-tested.

R9_responsiveness.criterion: The layout holds at a phone width, a tablet width and a desktop width.
R9_responsiveness.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the explorer, the account route and the home route each reflow cleanly at the three widths with no horizontal scrollbar. Answer no when any width produces overlapping content or a sideways scroll.
R9_responsiveness.rationale: The observations establish responsive reflow and directly rule out horizontal overflow only for the home route at phone width. They do not include direct scroll-width/overflow measurements for the solutions explorer and account routes at all three widths, nor for the home route at tablet and desktop widths. Since screenshots were unavailable for visual inspection, overlap or sideways scrolling cannot be conclusively excluded across every required route-width combination.
evidence: layout measurements captured
At 390×844, the supplied deterministic measurement for the home route reports bodyScrollWidth=390 and horizontalOverflow=false; its measured content generally collapses to viewport-width rows.
Fresh snapshots at 390×844 and 768×1024 showed responsive navigation replacing the desktop link row with an “Open the menu” button on the home, solutions explorer, and account routes.
Fresh snapshots confirmed the home, solutions explorer, and account route content remained present and traversable after resizing, including after vertical scrolling.
At 1440×900, the three routes loaded with desktop navigation and complete route content.

R10_ui_visual.criterion: The fixed top bar carries the logo lockup, the route labels and one Get in Touch action.
R10_ui_visual.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a slim bar across the top of every route holds the stacked-band logo beside the company name, the route labels and a single Get in Touch action. Answer no when the bar is missing one of the three, or when navigation sits in a side rail instead.
R10_ui_visual.rationale: Although the top navigation includes the logo/company lockup, route labels, and one header CTA, direct before/after scroll geometry shows that it is not fixed. Since the criterion explicitly requires a fixed top bar, the requirement is not met.
evidence: At 1920×1200 on `/`, the header area contains the Zettajoule lockup (ref 2), all nine route labels (refs 3–11), and one header-level `Get in Touch` action (ref 14). Their initial measured positions are at the top of the document: logo y=23–63, route labels y=0–86, and CTA y=25–61.

After pressing End, the same header elements measured far above the viewport: logo y=-2815–-2775, Company y=-2838–-2802, and header `Get in Touch` y=-2813–-2777. Thus the bar scrolls away rather than remaining fixed at the top.

The other `Get in Touch` (ref 28) measured at y=630–677 after scrolling to the end and belongs to lower-page content, while the sole header CTA was offscreen. This distinguishes the header action from the page-level duplicate.

R11_functionality.criterion: The first load holds a plain white cover until the reactor is ready to draw.
R11_functionality.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a first visit shows a white cover carrying a progress readout that lifts once the first screen is ready. Answer no when the first screen appears half-drawn, or when the cover lifts before the reactor can render.
R11_functionality.rationale: The browser navigation tool completes only after the page has loaded, so it did not expose the initial paint interval needed to directly verify whether a plain white progress cover appeared and lifted at the correct moment. The fully rendered screen and absence of a post-load progress readout do not prove that no transient cover existed. Therefore the criterion cannot be defensibly marked yes or no from the available observations.
evidence: no deterministic probe for composite; browser specialist required

On repeated direct navigations to unique variants of `/`, the first browser snapshot available after navigation already showed the complete home screen, including “Powering the World” and the reactor labels “Control rods,” “Dome,” “Core,” and “Base.”
No progress readout was present in any available post-navigation snapshot or visible-text capture.
CDP animation capture around multiple navigations detected only one running animation named `svelte-1uha8ag-zj-hint` (1600 ms), with no independently captured loader/cover transition.

R12_ux_flow.criterion: Every empty list on the account route states what is absent.
R12_ux_flow.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when an account with no saves, no searches and no applications sees a message on each list naming what is missing and offering a way onward. Answer no when an empty list renders as blank space.
R12_ux_flow.rationale: All three lists named by the evaluation rule were directly observed empty. Each explicitly states what is absent and provides a relevant way onward; none renders as blank space. The fixture mutation used to create the no-saves condition was restored.
evidence: On /account for visitor2@example.com, I temporarily removed the account's only saved solution and confirmed the resulting empty state rendered: “Saved solutions 0”, “No saved solutions yet.”, “Nothing has been kept from the explorer.”, with the onward link “Open the explorer”.
In that same no-saves account state, Saved searches rendered “0”, “No saved searches yet.”, “Filter the explorer and name the result to keep it.”, with the onward link “Filter the explorer”.
In that same no-saves account state, Job applications rendered “0”, “No applications sent.”, “Nothing has been applied for from this account.”, with the onward link “See the open jobs”.

The removal flow required confirmation (“Remove Mining from your saved solutions?” / “Yes, remove it”), then displayed confirmation “That saved solution is gone from your account.” I restored the reversible fixture afterward by saving Mining again and verified /account showed “Saved solutions 1” with Mining.
